description: A composite two-panel (a, b) X-ray diffraction figure of near-rapidly solidified low-density Fe-20Mn-9Al-1.2C-xCr steel strips. Both panels are stacked diffractograms with x-axis "Diffraction angle 2θ (degree)" spanning 30-100° and y-axis "Intensity(au)" carrying no numeric scale or tick values; each panel contains three vertically offset curves labelled 0Cr, 3Cr and 6Cr from bottom to top. (a) is the as-cast condition: peak labels read (111)γ (red), (220)DO3 (blue), (110)δ (green, arrowed) and (200)γ (red) in the 43-50° region, followed at higher angles by (200)δ, (220)γ, (211)δ, (311)γ and (222)γ. All three as-cast curves show a double peak between about 43.5° and 45.0°, and the relative weight of the (110)δ component visibly drops as Cr increases, consistent with the citing text that Cr promotes δ-ferrite → ordered DO3 transformation. (b) is the annealed condition: an additional (400)DO3 label appears near 65° beside (200)δ, and the 43.5-45.0° double peak collapses to essentially a single strong reflection whose relative intensity grows from 0Cr to 6Cr, indicating an increased DO3 content. No numeric intensities, d-spacings, indices' 2θ values or scale bars are printed.

subfigures.description: Stacked XRD patterns (Intensity(au) vs Diffraction angle 2θ = 30-100°) of as-cast 0Cr, 3Cr and 6Cr steel strips; peaks labelled (111)γ, (220)DO3, (110)δ, (200)γ near 43-50° and (200)δ, (220)γ, (211)δ, (311)γ, (222)γ at higher angles; a double peak between ~43.5° and 45.0° is present in all three curves, with the (110)δ contribution decreasing from 0Cr to 6Cr.

Stacked XRD patterns of the annealed 0Cr, 3Cr and 6Cr strips, same axes; in addition to (111)γ, (220)DO3, (110)δ, (200)γ, (220)γ, (211)δ, (311)γ and (222)γ, a (400)DO3 reflection is labelled near 2θ ≈ 65° next to (200)δ; the 43.5-45.0° double peak has become essentially a single peak whose relative intensity increases with Cr content.

observations.observation: Both panels plot stacked diffractograms with x-axis labelled "Diffraction angle 2θ (degree)" from 30 to 100 and y-axis labelled "Intensity(au)" with no numeric intensity ticks or scale bar.
Each panel contains three stacked curves labelled 0Cr (bottom), 3Cr (middle) and 6Cr (top), i.e. the Cr content of the Fe-20Mn-9Al-1.2C-xCr steel strips.
Panel (a) shows as-cast strips and panel (b) annealed strips, per the caption "(a) as-cast; (b) annealed".

Panel (a) peak labels visible in the 43-50° range are (111)γ (red), (220)DO3 (blue), (110)δ (green, arrowed) and (200)γ (red); at higher angles the labels read (200)δ, (220)γ, (211)δ, (311)γ and (222)γ in blue.
The as-cast patterns display a double peak between 43.5° and 45.0°, identified in the citing text as (110)δ plus (220)DO3 with space group Fm3m and lattice parameter a = 0.565 nm in the ferrite.

The citing text states the area ratio of the (110)δ peak to the (220)DO3 peak gradually decreases with increasing Cr content, so Cr promotes the transformation from δ-ferrite to the ordered DO3 phase.
Visually, the relative height of the left-most (lower-2θ) peak of the doublet in (a) decreases from the 0Cr curve to the 6Cr curve, while the second component is relatively unchanged.

The citing text states the double peak between 43.5° and 45.0° changes into a single peak when the strips are annealed at 600 °C for 3 h, indicating that almost all the ferrite transforms into the ordered DO3 phase.
In panel (b) an extra label (400)DO3 appears near 2θ ≈ 65° alongside (200)δ, i.e. a DO3 superlattice-type reflection is annotated only in the annealed condition.
The citing text states the intensity of the single peak is significantly enhanced with increasing Cr content in the annealed strips, indicating that the DO3 phase content does increase.

Visually, in (b) the peak near 2θ ≈ 44-45° becomes progressively more prominent relative to the neighbouring peak at ~43.5° from 0Cr through 3Cr to 6Cr, matching the reported increase of the DO3 single peak with Cr.

The citing text states the steel strips mainly consist of austenite and ferrite, the ferrite being high-temperature δ-ferrite retained because of the high cooling rate during near-rapid solidification [30].
No numeric peak positions, intensities, d-spacings or lattice parameters appear as labels in either panel; all quantitative statements about peak ratios come from the citing text, not the pixels.

unreadable_items: Exact 2θ positions of the labelled peaks are not printed (no numeric tick labels for individual peaks); peak positions can only be read approximately against the 10°-spaced axis ticks
y-axis intensity has no numeric values (arbitrary units), so no peak intensities or area ratios can be quantified from the pixels
Small high-angle peak labels (e.g. (200)δ, (211)δ) are rendered at low size and are only partially readable at the supplied resolution
